The stored identity of the app (machine GUID, computer name, install date, product ID, volume serial) is also applied to the lab prefix, so Battle.net sees the same device as the game. The game and the stored identity are not changed. The log shows only short IDs.

This removes the lab prefix, the installer, downloads and logs (%1$s MB). The game and its folder stay as they are. Loaded Wine and FEX packages stay.
The lab cannot be deleted while a run is active. End it first.
Removes the Lab entry from the Help page. Tap the version line seven times to show it again.
One run, six steps: starts the lab, lists the L: drive, checks the helper programs, runs a built-in 32-bit program and then the installer. The result goes into the report.
Step test: all 6 steps ran to the end.
Step test: ended after step %1$d (installer missing).
Step test: last step reached: %1$d of 6, finished up to step %2$d.
Step test: no step reached (the batch never ran).
Direct starts the program the way the game starts its ARM64 program. winhandler.exe is a 64-bit Intel helper and needs a translator for 64-bit Intel programs, which choice 1 does not have.
Used when Own value is chosen, for example err+all,+relay. Separate parts with commas.
bad WINEDEBUG value (parts like err+all, +process or -all, separated by commas): %1$s
Choice 1 runs only 32-bit Intel programs. 64-bit Intel programs (such as winhandler.exe) need another translator.
Saved login details are never typed in the lab. Enter them by hand.

%1$s is already installed. Nothing was loaded again. To use it, choose it under Settings (for FEX: quick pick 2).
Translator: FEX is chosen, but there is no usable package
The FEX package %1$s is installed but not chosen: the next start still uses the bundled translator. Tap the button below to choose it.
FEX is chosen, but no FEX package is installed. Load fex-2508 under Packages first. The start is refused until then.
FEX is chosen, but no FEX version is picked. Pick one under Settings. The start is refused until then.
The chosen FEX version %1$s is not installed. The start is refused until you pick an installed one.
The chosen Wine package %1$s is not installed. The start is refused until you pick an installed one.
Without a translator, Intel programs do not run (counter-test only).
Stage 0 changes nothing (behaviour as before). Uses the bundled translator.
Stage 1 sets three Box64 values (SAFEFLAGS, STRONGMEM, ALIGNED_ATOMICS), the ones the public Box64 uses for Battle.net.exe. Uses the bundled translator.
Stage 2 is stage 1 plus the start switch --js-flags=--jitless for Battle.net (no JIT code in the browser engine). Uses the bundled translator.
Stage 3 sets all values of the app preset STABILITY of Box64, plus ALIGNED_ATOMICS=0. Uses the bundled translator.
Stage 4 chooses the translator FEX with its normal settings. This combination ran without crashes in tests on the device.
Stage 5 chooses the translator FEX with the values of the app preset STABILITY of FEX. Slower; only if stage 4 crashes.
Stage 4 needs an installed FEX package. Load fex-2508 under Packages first.
Stability stage %1$d (%2$s) chosen. It applies to the next start.
FEX is no longer chosen: the stability stage is back to 1.
Signing in: if the first sign-in window is drawn incompletely, tap the gear icon at its top right, choose to continue without logging in, and sign in from the main window.
Your own lines under Settings still win over the lines of the stage.
Sets BOX64_LOG=1 and BOX64_DYNAREC_MISSING=1 for lab starts only (not for the game). The log gets longer.
No run yet. Every run adds one entry here (newest first, at most 10).
The lab never sees the game folder itself, only a complete copy of it. The game folder is only read, never changed.
No game folder found. There is nothing to copy.
%1$d links or special files are skipped and not copied.
Free space for the copy: %1$s GB, needed: %2$s GB (size plus 2 GB reserve).
Not enough space: the button is locked. %1$s GB more are needed.
An unfinished copy exists. It is never used by the lab. Continue copy resumes it and skips files that are already complete.

%1$d files (%2$s GB) are copied from the game folder into the lab storage. Free space: %3$s GB, needed: %4$s GB. The game folder is only read. Copying can take a long time; you can cancel and continue later.
Copying started. The screen may turn off; the copy goes on.
Copy cancelled. A later Continue copy skips the files that are complete.
The copy stopped: a file could not be written or read.
The copy stopped: a file of the game folder changed while it was read. Start it again.
The copy stopped: the check afterwards found a missing file. Start it again.
The copy was refused: the target and the game folder overlap.
A lab run is active or the copy is running. Try again afterwards.
This removes only the copy in the lab storage. The game folder stays as it is.
The copy could not be deleted.
Adds the finished copy to the lab as drive K:. The original game folder is never added. Off by default.
No complete copy yet, so nothing is added.

Unverified: Battle.net does not find the copy with Locate the game. Choose Install instead and pick drive K: as the install location. The launcher adds the folder World of Warcraft by itself and should take over the existing data. If it downloads everything again, cancel. This has not been tested on a device.

The copy is complete. Refreshing copies the files from the game folder again where they are missing or differ (%1$d files, %2$s GB in total; free space: %3$s GB, needed: %4$s GB). Files the launcher added to the copy stay. Files that exist in both and differ are replaced by the game folder version. The game folder is only read. For a full fresh start use Delete copy.
The copy stopped: the existing copy could not be moved into the folder World of Warcraft (%1$s). Nothing was deleted and the copy is not mounted.
The existing copy could not be moved into the folder World of Warcraft (%1$s). It is not mounted and nothing was deleted. Open this page again to retry.
Checked before and after every lab run: unchanged (last check %1$s).
Checked before and after every lab run. No run has been checked yet.
The original game folder was changed during the last lab run. Details are in the protocol. Further lab starts are locked until you confirm.
Confirmed. Lab starts are possible again.
The last lab run changed the original game folder. Confirm first under Advanced, Game folder and space (red block).
The game copy is being created. Wait for it or cancel it first.
Set up the sign-in path: bundled Wine, FEX, stage 4, game copy off
Sign-in setup set: bundled Wine, FEX (%1$s), stage 4, game copy off. The Game switch in the key bar starts off in every run. It applies to the next start.
The setting for signing in needs the translator (%1$s). Nothing was changed and nothing loads by itself. Load it under Advanced, Technical, then set the setting again.
To load it: open Advanced, Technical
Do not try to sign in again and again: after a rejection, wait instead of repeating.
The launcher is software of the vendor. This app does not type credentials and does not read sign-in values.
From experience on one device (may change with launcher updates): if the first sign-in window is drawn wrongly, tap the gear, choose Continue without logging in, then sign in in the main window.
If sign-in is refused: close Battle.net on your PC or sign out there, then try once more (untested tip). Do not retry sign-ins repeatedly.
Set up Battle.net: guide and settings
The lab could not be prepared. Nothing was started. Try again; if it happens again, share the lab report.

All steps done. Start the launcher to play

The last start ended without a window or with an error window. Restarting helped on the test device most of the time (experience from one device, not proven). Nothing restarts by itself.
Signing in needs a small component of the app, the translator. It is loaded once.
Battle.net has to be installed once. The setup program comes from the vendor; this app loads and starts it.
One tap sets everything the way it worked on the test device. The switch for the copy of the game stays as it is.
Start Battle.net and sign in yourself. This app never types or reads your credentials.
Optional. A copy of the game gives Battle.net a place to install into. Without it you can only sign in.
In Battle.net choose Install and pick the copy of the game (drive K:) as the location.
Start Battle.net and press Play there. The game controls switch on by themselves as soon as the game window is active.

Experience from one device (may change with updates): choose Install, location K:. Battle.net appends the folder World of Warcraft by itself and then downloads about 1 GB; that took about 8 minutes without anything changing in its windows.

Adds the buttons E-mail and Password to the key bar for the Battle.net start. A tap types the login saved in the game area settings into the field you tapped before. Off by default.
On your tap, the app types exactly one saved value into the field you tapped before. It does not check which field that is. Do not try to sign in again and again: after a rejection, wait.

%1$d characters cannot be sent, please type them by hand

From a test run on one device (experience, not a guarantee): set up the authenticator for your account. For the first few times, until the game starts stably, sign in to the Battle.net launcher with the e-mail code (the e-mail code option in the sign-in window). There the password was not accepted at first, the e-mail code worked reliably. Do not try sign-ins again and again.
Unofficial: signing in is at your own risk.
%1$s: nothing to tap here right now. The reason is in the row.

Battle.net does not respond. Restart it?
Battle.net was closed at your request. Start it again? Wait a few seconds if the start is refused.
Signed in. You can now start the game directly.

On some devices the provider refuses the sign-in inside the game (an “Are you a robot?” check, error BLZ51914400). Signing in once in the real Battle.net program on this device helped in our test (one device). Whether signing in alone is enough is not confirmed.
If the direct start is still refused: do not repeat it. Set up part B and start via Battle.net instead.
Part B: If the direct start is refused
A copy of the game and its installation in the Battle.net program. Needs about 50 GB extra, and starting takes longer.
Off: Advanced is closed every time the page opens. On: it is open, with only the first group open.
More hints on signing in are under Advanced, Sign-in.
Order of steps if the in-game sign-in is refused
Sign in to the Battle.net app for Android (it also holds the authenticator).
Sign in to battle.net in the browser on this device.
Sign in here in the Battle.net program, preferably with an e-mail code. If Battle.net is running on your PC: sign out there.
If that does not help: tap “Install” for the game once in the Battle.net program. Whether a started download is enough has not been checked; it uses storage.
Then start the game directly from the home screen. One attempt, do not repeat.
Steps 1 to 3 helped in our test (one device). Step 4 is a guess.
Copy of the game and storage.
Wine is the layer that runs Windows programs on Android.
The translator turns Intel instructions into ones for this device; FEX is the one the sign-in relies on.
Packages are components (Wine, translator) that the app downloads.
For developers only: free input that changes the start. Mistakes here can make Battle.net unusable.
All settings of this page go back to the defaults. Loaded packages, the copy of the game and your answers in the steps stay.
